newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate unchanged in tight market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate unchanged in tight market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 8.50/70 percent on Wednesday as the market continued to be tight, dealers said.
They said there was little activity and demand was mainly from small institutions considered higher risk borrowers in the market.
"It's pretty quiet. People are just waiting what the central bank would do," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "The market is still looking for direction."
Bank Negara has been injecting fresh funds over the past two weeks, but dealers said it was not enough to ease the market which was too short.
"The lending has been in small amounts, probably because Bank Negara did not want rates to come down too fast," one dealer said.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
A big local bank is said to be lending one-month money on behalf of the central bank this morning.
There was no confirmation of the funds injection from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its market operations.
Earlier, interbank rates were also steady due to market tightness, caused partly by month-end ringgit demand.
One-, two- and three-week money were all unchanged at 8.50/70 percent.
One-month money was steady at 8.50 percent and three-month at 8.00/30 percent.
Dealers said rates might come off slightly at the end of the week due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were down across the board to reflect firmness in interbank rates.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down three points to 92.23, or an implied yield of 7.77 percent.
The December contract fell two to 92.48, or 7.52 percent while March 1998 was also down two to 92.57, or 7.43 percent.
